description:
FOUND s438i (Opus 5), exposed by #450 -- before that fix a no-wildcard pattern
that matched nothing returned an EMPTY vector every time, so no iterator state
was ever created and the divergence could not be seen.

  my $a = glob("/nope-abc");
  my $b = glob("/nope-abc");
  # perl: a=[/nope-abc] b=[/nope-abc]      PCL: a=[/nope-abc] b=[U]

perl's scalar-context glob iterator belongs to the OP -- each `glob` CALL SITE
has its own -- which is what makes `while (my $f = glob("*.c"))` terminate
without one call site poisoning another.  `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`'s
`*p-glob-iterators*` is a global hash keyed by the PATTERN STRING, so two
independent call sites share one iterator: the second sees `:scalar-done` and
answers nil.

THE COST, measured: t/op/glob.t row 18 ("Make sure the presence of the
CORE::GLOBAL::glob typeglob does not affect whether File::Glob::csh_glob is
called") compares `$output1 eq $output2` from two separate `eval q{ glob(...) }`
call sites.  It PASSED before #450 because both were undef -- an accidental
pass on nothing, the same family as the two rows the s435 flip exposed -- and
now fails honestly.  The snapshot row is edited to 13/5 with this cause.

FIX SHAPE: the iterator key must carry a CALL-SITE identity, which the emission
does not have today.  Options, cheapest first:
 (a) emit a per-site constant with the call -- `(p-glob PAT :site N)` -- and key
     the hash on (site . pat).  The site id is a compile-time counter; every
     glob emitter (gen_readline_form's glob branch, the p-glob builtin path,
     the `<*.c>` form) must pass it, so it is a small change in several places.
 (b) key on the CL source location if one is reachable at run time -- fragile,
     and the readline/glob forms are macro-expanded.
(a) is the shape perl itself has.

BAR: the two-call probe above; `while (my $f = glob("*"))` must still terminate
(that is what the current keying buys); t/op/glob.t back to 14/4; `cl/` change,
so the full sweep plus the io/ and op/ companion dirs.
subject: The scalar-context glob ITERATOR is keyed by PATTERN, where perl keys it by CALL SITE: two independent `glob("/x")` calls give the value then UNDEF (perl gives it twice)
